notes: App lifecycle maps to Tauri's App and AppHandle; event names differ slightly.
Standard paths (home, app data, documents) map to Tauri's core path API — no plugin needed.
Direct equivalent; exit code handling is the same.
Window options (size, title, frame, resizable) map to WebviewWindowBuilder.
Each handler becomes a Tauri command registered with invoke_handler.
Fire-and-forget main-side listeners map to Tauri events.
Request/response calls map one-to-one to Tauri invoke().
Renderer event listeners map to Tauri listen().
Fire-and-forget renderer sends map to Tauri emit().
File picker options map closely; multi-select and filters are supported.
Save dialog maps directly; default path handling differs slightly.
Message boxes map directly; button order follows platform conventions.
Generic dialog use — check which dialog call this is; most map to the dialog plugin.
Generic shell use — openExternal/openPath map to the opener plugin; check the call site.
Generic webContents use (navigation guards, JS evaluation, window-open handling) — check the call site; Tauri equivalents vary by call.
Static templates convert mechanically; dynamic menus and roles need review.
Menu items map over, but Electron roles have no one-to-one Tauri equivalent.
Tray icons need the plugin and per-platform icon assets; context menus differ.
Opening URLs in the default browser is a direct plugin call.
Opening files and folders maps directly to the opener plugin.
Desktop notifications map directly; action buttons need capability config.
Global hotkeys map to the plugin; accelerator strings are mostly identical.
Custom schemes are possible in Tauri but the registration API is different.
Electron sessions have no Tauri equivalent; cookie and partition logic needs a redesign.
OS keychain access works via the keyring crate, but the API shape differs.
Dark/light theme detection and switching map to the Tauri window API.
Auto-updates need the plugin plus a signed update feed; the flow is similar.
Main-to-renderer messages map to Tauri window events.
DevTools toggling is a direct window method in Tauri.
Clipboard read/write maps to the plugin; image clipboard support varies by OS.
Display enumeration maps to Tauri's monitor API.
No direct Tauri equivalent; power events need a platform-specific Rust implementation.
No built-in Tauri crash reporter; use a service SDK (e.g. Sentry) instead.
Electron's net maps to reqwest in Rust, but the streaming API differs.
Image loading and resizing need the image crate or Tauri's image helpers.
Exposed preload APIs become a thin shim calling Tauri invoke().
JSON key-value storage maps to the Tauri store plugin; file location differs.
Pseudo-terminals need the portable-pty crate and a hand-written command layer.
Synchronous SQLite access becomes rusqlite calls behind Tauri commands.
Single-instance lock and second-instance argv handling map to the plugin; the focus/restore logic still needs porting.
Deep-link protocol registration maps to the plugin; the open-url / second-instance URL handling still needs porting.
A Tauri webview has no Node.js runtime: renderer code that imports `electron` or Node builtins cannot run unmodified and needs a rewrite against the Tauri bridge.
contextIsolation: false lets renderer code reach Node/Electron globals directly; the Tauri bridge replaces that access, so the renderer needs review.
The remote module was removed from Electron itself and has no Tauri equivalent; every remote call must become an explicit invoke() + Rust command.
Auto-updates need the plugin plus a signed update feed; the flow is similar.
Window position/size persistence maps to the plugin; defaultWidth/defaultHeight carry over as the window's initial size.
The remote package has no Tauri equivalent; every remote call must become an explicit invoke() + Rust command.
Async SQLite access becomes rusqlite calls behind Tauri commands.
Chromium command-line switches have no Tauri equivalent; each switch needs a per-app decision (drop it, or pass it to the webview where the webview supports it).
The macOS dock API (setMenu, bounce, show/hide) has no Tauri core equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
Dock/taskbar badge counts have no Tauri core equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
The Windows AppUserModelID has no Tauri core equivalent; set it from Rust platform code or the Windows app manifest.
Windows jump lists have no Tauri core equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
Enabling Chromium's sandbox has no Tauri equivalent — Tauri webviews are sandboxed by the platform webview, so the call is usually droppable, but verify per app.
The packaged-vs-dev check has no Tauri equivalent; use the Tauri dev/release build distinction (tauri::is_dev() / cfg(debug_assertions)) instead.
The ARM-translation check has no Tauri equivalent; use std::env::consts::ARCH in Rust instead.
Login-item (start at login) settings have no Tauri core equivalent; needs platform Rust code or the tauri-plugin-autostart plugin.
Reading login-item settings has no Tauri core equivalent; use the tauri-plugin-autostart plugin's query API.
Renaming the app at runtime has no Tauri equivalent; the app name comes from tauri.conf.json instead.
Redirecting a standard path (e.g. userData) has no Tauri equivalent; the path API does not support overriding the app-data directory.
Moving the app into /Applications (macOS) has no Tauri equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
Checking whether the app lives in /Applications (macOS) has no Tauri equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
Disabling Chromium hardware acceleration has no Tauri equivalent; the system webview manages its own rendering.
Preferred system languages have no Tauri core equivalent; read the OS locale from Rust instead.
The Linux desktop-file name has no Tauri equivalent; it comes from the bundle metadata instead.
Redirecting the app-logs path has no Tauri equivalent; point the logger at the path directly instead.
Querying the default protocol handler maps to the deep-link plugin alongside registration; the open-url handling still needs porting.
Removing a protocol registration maps to the deep-link plugin alongside registration.
DNS resolution is not HTTP: reqwest cannot do it. Use a DNS resolver crate (e.g. hickory-resolver) or std::net::ToSocketAddrs.
The connectivity check is not an HTTP request: reqwest is the wrong shape. Use a connectivity check (e.g. a DNS probe or the online crate).
Electron's net.fetch maps to reqwest in Rust, but the streaming API differs.
Electron's net.request maps to reqwest in Rust, but the streaming API differs.
Embedding a webview inside a window has no Tauri equivalent; it is a redesign (separate WebviewWindow or a webview tag replacement).

The <webview> tag (and the webviewTag webPreference) embeds a guest page inside a window; Tauri has no webview tag — it is a redesign (a separate WebviewWindow, or the guest content served as a route in the same webview).
Utility processes have no Tauri equivalent; use a Rust sidecar (tauri-plugin-shell sidecar) instead.
MessagePort plumbing between main and renderer has no Tauri equivalent; replace with Tauri events/commands.
Screen/window capture-source enumeration has no Tauri equivalent; needs a platform plugin (screen capture).
OS preferences (macOS defaults, media-access status, accent color, notification subscriptions) have no Tauri equivalent; needs platform Rust code.
Renderer-frame controls (zoom level, spell-checker provider) map to the Tauri webview API, but not one-to-one; check the call site.
File-drop path resolution has no direct Tauri equivalent; Tauri drag-drop events carry file paths instead.
Chromium tracing (startRecording/stopRecording, heap profiling) has no Tauri equivalent.
Each one-shot handler becomes a Tauri command registered with invoke_handler, like ipcMain.handle.
Remote-only: reading a main-process global from the renderer has no Tauri equivalent; expose the value through an invoke() + Rust command instead.
Remote-only: the current BrowserWindow from the renderer has no Tauri equivalent; use the Tauri window API in the webview instead.
Remote-only: the current WebContents from the renderer has no Tauri equivalent; use the Tauri webview API instead.
Setting the application menu maps to the Tauri menu API (app.set_menu()); platform conventions need a human look.
DIP conversion needs manual math from the monitor's scaleFactor; the monitor API gives the scale factor but not the conversion.
tauri_target: tauri window / monitor API (scaleFactor + manual DIP math)

notes: Forcing a renderer crash has no Tauri equivalent.
Checking whether the renderer crashed has no Tauri equivalent; the webview's lifecycle events are the closest signal.
Native keychain bindings become keyring-crate calls behind Tauri commands.
The sqlite-vec vector-search extension becomes rusqlite with the sqlite-vec extension loaded.
Signal's SQLCipher addon becomes rusqlite with SQLCipher (or sqlx with the sqlcipher feature) behind Tauri commands.
Privileged file operations (admin elevation) have no Tauri equivalent; needs a Rust port with platform elevation.
Windows registry access becomes the winreg crate behind Tauri commands.
llama.cpp bindings are a native addon (model loading, GPU/CPU inference); needs a Rust port (e.g. llama.cpp bindings or a sidecar).
